key_terms.meaning: fck or fy value below which not more than 5% of test results fall.
Design moment obtained by applying partial safety factors to characteristic loads.
Distance from extreme compression fibre to centroid of tension steel.
Depth of concrete in compression measured from extreme compression fibre.
Idealised concrete stress distribution at collapse; resultant 0.36 fck b xu acts at 0.42 xu from compression face.
z = d − 0.42 xu, distance between concrete compression and steel tension resultants.
Section where tension steel reaches yield strain exactly when concrete reaches ultimate strain.
Section with Ast less than balanced steel; steel yields before concrete crushes.
Section with Ast greater than balanced steel; concrete crushes before steel yields.
Moment capacity when xu = xu,max; for Fe415 about 0.138 fck bd².
Beam with compression steel Asc and tension steel Ast, used when Mu exceeds Mu,lim or depth is restricted.
Stress in compression steel at collapse, found from strain compatibility and the design stress-strain curve.
T- or L-section formed by a slab cast monolithically with a beam.
Limited width of slab assumed to act with the web in compression.
Tables and charts giving steel percentage or moment capacity for given fck, fy and Mu/bd².
Limit state of deflection, cracking or vibration under service loads.
Checking vertical deflection at service loads by limits or span/depth rules.
Limiting crack width by bar spacing, cover and steel distribution.
Moment at which extreme concrete tension reaches flexural tensile strength and first crack forms.
Elastic section with steel replaced by an equivalent area of concrete, m times steel area.
m = Es/Ec, ratio of steel modulus to concrete modulus.

takeaways: In limit state design, the factored moment is resisted by an internal couple between the concrete compression block and the tension steel.
The neutral axis depth follows from horizontal equilibrium and strain compatibility, and it must not exceed xu,max for a ductile section.
The steel percentage relative to the balanced value decides whether steel yields first, concrete crushes first, or both occur together.
When Mu exceeds Mu,lim or depth is restricted, compression steel and extra tension steel form a second internal couple.
A monolithic slab can act as a compression flange only over a limited effective width.
Design aids replace repetitive quadratic solutions with direct tables and charts, but the designer still checks ductility and detailing.
Strength checks alone are not enough; deflection and crack width must satisfy serviceability limits at service loads.
Before cracking, a transformed section gives elastic stresses and the cracking moment Mcr.
bank_note: Long answers usually combine the stress-block derivation with IS 456 checks for singly, doubly and flanged beams, then finish with design-aid use and serviceability checks.

bank.q: State the assumptions of limit state design for flexure and derive the expressions for the concrete compression force and lever arm for a singly reinforced rectangular beam.
outline: List assumptions: plane sections remain plane, concrete tensile strength ignored, stress block idealised.
Write compression force C = 0.36 fck b xu.
Write tension force T = 0.87 fy Ast.
Use equilibrium C = T to locate xu.
Write lever arm z = d − 0.42 xu and Mu = T z.

bank.q: Explain balanced, under-reinforced and over-reinforced sections using strain and stress diagrams. Give the failure mode of each.
outline: Draw strain diagram with concrete ultimate strain and steel yield strain.
Define balanced section: both reach limiting strains together.
Define under-reinforced section: steel yields before concrete crushes.
Define over-reinforced section: concrete crushes before steel yields.
State that IS 456 favours under-reinforced ductile sections.

bank.q: Define limiting moment of resistance Mu,lim. Derive its expression for a rectangular section and state the values of xu,max/d for Fe250, Fe415 and Fe500.
outline: Define Mu,lim as capacity when xu = xu,max.
Use C = 0.36 fck b xu,max.
Use z = d − 0.42 xu,max.
Write Mu,lim = 0.36 fck b xu,max (d − 0.42 xu,max).
State xu,max/d values: 0.53, 0.48 and 0.46.

bank.q: Why is compression steel provided in a beam? Explain how a doubly reinforced section resists moment greater than Mu,lim.
outline: State reasons: Mu exceeds Mu,lim, depth restriction, deflection control.
Concrete alone reaches Mu,lim at xu,max.
Extra tension steel balances compression steel.
Compression steel and extra tension steel form an additional couple.
Total Mu = Mu,lim plus additional moment from the steel couple.

bank.q: A simply supported rectangular beam of span 5 m carries a factored moment of 120 kN m. Take b = 250 mm, d = 450 mm, fck = 25 N/mm² and fy = 500 N/mm². Design the tension steel and check xu/d against the limiting value.
outline: Compute Mu/bd² and compare with Mu,lim/bd².
Confirm section can be singly reinforced.
Solve Ast from Mu = 0.87 fy Ast (d − 0.42 xu).
Use design aid or quadratic solution.
Check xu/d ≤ xu,max/d and check minimum and maximum steel.

bank.q: A rectangular beam 300 mm wide and 600 mm deep has to resist a factored moment of 350 kN m, but the effective depth is restricted to 450 mm. Design compression and tension steel using fck = 30 N/mm² and fy = 415 N/mm².
outline: Compare Mu with Mu,lim for the restricted depth.
Find Mu2 = Mu − Mu,lim.
Assume compression steel stress from strain compatibility.
Compute Asc from Mu2 = Asc fsc (d − d′).
Compute total Ast = Ast1 + Ast2 and check limits.

bank.q: A T-beam has web width 300 mm, flange thickness 100 mm, effective depth 550 mm and effective flange width 1200 mm. It carries a factored moment of 400 kN m with fck = 25 N/mm² and fy = 415 N/mm². Determine whether the flange acts as a full compression flange and design the tension steel.
outline: First assume neutral axis lies within flange.
Check whether 0.36 fck bf Df can supply required compression.
If xu exceeds Df, use flanged stress block with web and flange contributions.
Compute Ast from equilibrium and lever arm.
Check xu/d ≤ xu,max/d and detailing rules.

bank.q: Explain how design aid tables in SP 16 are used to choose tension steel for a rectangular beam. Illustrate with Mu = 150 kN m, b = 300 mm, d = 500 mm, fck = 25 N/mm² and fy = 415 N/mm².
outline: Compute Mu/bd².
Enter the appropriate SP 16 table for fck and fy.
Read steel percentage pt or Ast/bd.
Interpolate between table values if needed.
Check pt against limiting value and provide bars.

bank.q: A rectangular beam of b = 300 mm and D = 500 mm has 3 bars of 16 mm diameter at effective cover 50 mm. Take fck = 25 N/mm². Calculate the cracking moment and the concrete and steel stresses just before cracking using a transformed section.
outline: Compute Ast and modular ratio m = Es/Ec.
Transform steel to equivalent concrete area mAst.
Locate elastic neutral axis by taking moments of areas.
Compute gross moment of inertia of transformed section.
Use Mcr = fcr I / yt and compute stresses from My/I.

bank.q: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries service loads that give a service moment of 100 kN m. The section is 250 mm × 500 mm with 3 bars of 16 mm. Check deflection by span/depth rule and crack control by IS 456 bar-spacing provisions.
outline: Compute effective depth and span/depth ratio.
Apply IS 456 deflection limits for the support condition.
Check bar spacing against crack control rules.
Check cover and distribution of tension steel.
State whether serviceability is satisfied or needs revision.

bank.q: An over-reinforced beam is proposed because steel is cheaper than concrete. Evaluate this choice using IS 456 provisions and failure mode.
outline: Explain that over-reinforced section fails by concrete crushing.
State sudden brittle failure and lack of warning.
Compare with under-reinforced ductile behaviour.
Refer to IS 456 limits on xu/d and steel percentage.
Recommend redesign as under-reinforced or doubly reinforced.

bank.q: Evaluate the effect of slab participation on the capacity of a T-beam. Why is the effective flange width limited?
outline: Explain monolithic slab and beam action.
State that full slab width does not carry uniform compression.
Define effective flange width from IS 456.
Discuss shear lag and variation of stress across flange.
Show that limited bf gives safe design capacity.

bank.q: A shallow beam passes the strength check but shows excessive deflection and cracks. Analyse the causes and give remedies.
outline: Check span/depth ratio and serviceability limits.
Discuss low stiffness and high service stress.
Relate cracking to steel stress, cover and bar spacing.
Suggest increasing depth, adding compression steel or revising bars.
Recheck deflection and crack control after revision.

bank.q: For a given beam layout and loads, compare singly reinforced, doubly reinforced and flanged options, then recommend a section and check serviceability.
outline: Estimate factored moment and Mu,lim for available sections.
Compare singly reinforced capacity with demand.
Discuss doubly reinforced option when depth is restricted.
Discuss T-beam option when slab acts monolithically.
Recommend section and check deflection and cracking.

glossary.def: The strength value below which not more than 5% of test results are expected to fall.
The value obtained by dividing characteristic strength by the partial safety factor for material.
A multiplier that accounts for uncertainty in loads or material strength.
A load obtained by multiplying a characteristic load by the partial safety factor for loads.
A condition beyond which a structure no longer satisfies its design requirements.
An idealised shape of concrete stress at collapse used to compute compression force.
The limiting neutral axis depth for a ductile section with a given steel grade.
The steel percentage that makes steel yield exactly when concrete crushes.
A beam with tension steel only and no designed compression steel.
A beam with both compression steel and tension steel designed to resist moment.
A beam in which part of a monolithic slab acts as a compression flange.
The limited slab width assumed to act with the beam web in compression.
The vertical part of a flanged beam below the slab flange.
The horizontal slab part of a T- or L-beam that provides compression area.
A table or chart that gives steel percentage or moment capacity directly.
The ability of a structure to remain usable under service loads without excessive deflection or cracking.
Vertical movement of a beam under load, checked against span limits.
The width of a visible crack at the concrete surface, checked for durability and appearance.
The bending moment at which the extreme concrete fibre reaches its flexural tensile strength.
An elastic section in which steel area is replaced by an equivalent concrete area.
The ratio of modulus of elasticity of steel to that of concrete.
The perpendicular distance between the compression and tension resultants in a section.
The maximum moment a singly reinforced section can carry when the neutral axis is at xu,max.
A section in which tension steel yields before concrete reaches crushing strain.
A section in which concrete crushes before tension steel yields.
